# Part II: Student Absences Analysis

## 2. Description, Source, and Exploration of the Data

### 2.1 Basic data information

```{r data}
student <- read.csv("student-por.csv", stringsAsFactors = TRUE)

dim(student)
str(student)
colSums(is.na(student))
```

### 2.2 Response: absences

```{r response}
summary(student$absences)

resp_summary <- data.frame(
  n        = length(student$absences),
  Mean     = mean(student$absences),
  Variance = var(student$absences),
  Ratio    = var(student$absences) / mean(student$absences),
  Pct_Zero = mean(student$absences == 0) * 100
)
kable(resp_summary, digits = 2,
      caption = "Summary of the response variable (absences)")

table(student$absences)
```

```{r fig1, fig.cap="Figure 1: Distribution of absences"}
ggplot(student, aes(x = absences)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "grey60", color = "black") +
  labs(x = "Number of Absences", y = "Number of Students") +
  theme_bw()
```

### 2.3 Predictors

```{r predictors}
walc_tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(student$absences, student$Walc), function(x)
  c(n = length(x), Mean = mean(x), Variance = var(x))))
kable(walc_tab, digits = 2,
      caption = "Table 1: Absences by weekend alcohol use (Walc)")

table(student$Walc)
table(student$Dalc)
table(student$studytime)
table(student$failures)
table(student$sex)
table(student$school)
summary(student$age)
```

```{r fig2, fig.cap="Figure 2: Absences by weekend alcohol consumption (red diamond = mean)"}
ggplot(student, aes(x = factor(Walc), y = absences)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "grey80") +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "point", shape = 18, size = 3, color = "red") +
  labs(x = "Weekend Alcohol Use (1 = very low, 5 = very high)",
       y = "Number of Absences") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r collinearity}
# Correlation between weekday and weekend alcohol use
cor(student$Dalc, student$Walc)
```

## 3. Proposed Analyses

```{r model-formula}
library(MASS)

model_formula <- absences ~ Walc + studytime + failures + sex + age + school
```

## 4. Analysis Results

### 4.1 Poisson regression

```{r poisson}
pois_model <- glm(model_formula, family = poisson(link = "log"), data = student)
summary(pois_model)
```

### 4.2 Overdispersion check

```{r dispersion}
pearson_chi2 <- sum(residuals(pois_model, type = "pearson")^2)

disp_tab <- data.frame(
  Statistic = c("Deviance", "Pearson Chi-square"),
  Value     = c(deviance(pois_model), pearson_chi2),
  df        = df.residual(pois_model),
  Ratio     = c(deviance(pois_model), pearson_chi2) / df.residual(pois_model)
)
kable(disp_tab, digits = 2, caption = "Table 2: Poisson goodness-of-fit and dispersion")

mu_hat  <- fitted(pois_model)
y       <- student$absences
ct_test <- lm(((y - mu_hat)^2 - y) / mu_hat ~ mu_hat - 1)
summary(ct_test)$coefficients
```

### 4.3 Negative binomial regression

```{r negbin}
nb_model <- glm.nb(model_formula, data = student)
summary(nb_model)

c(theta = nb_model$theta, SE_theta = nb_model$SE.theta, alpha = 1 / nb_model$theta)
```

### 4.4 Poisson vs. negative binomial

```{r compare}
lr_stat <- as.numeric(2 * (logLik(nb_model) - logLik(pois_model)))
lr_p    <- 0.5 * pchisq(lr_stat, df = 1, lower.tail = FALSE)
c(LR = lr_stat, p_value = lr_p)

fit_tab <- data.frame(
  Model      = c("Poisson", "Negative Binomial"),
  LogLik     = c(logLik(pois_model), logLik(nb_model)),
  AIC        = c(AIC(pois_model), AIC(nb_model)),
  BIC        = c(BIC(pois_model), BIC(nb_model)),
  Pearson_df = c(pearson_chi2 / df.residual(pois_model),
                 sum(residuals(nb_model, type = "pearson")^2) / df.residual(nb_model))
)
kable(fit_tab, digits = 2, caption = "Table 3: Model comparison")

se_tab <- data.frame(
  Poisson_Est = coef(pois_model),
  Poisson_SE  = sqrt(diag(vcov(pois_model))),
  NB_Est      = coef(nb_model),
  NB_SE       = sqrt(diag(vcov(nb_model)))
)
kable(se_tab, digits = 3, caption = "Table 4: Coefficient estimates and standard errors")
```

```{r fig3, fig.cap="Figure 3: Observed vs. predicted distribution of absences"}
max_y <- 15
obs_freq  <- sapply(0:max_y, function(k) mean(y == k))
pois_freq <- sapply(0:max_y, function(k) mean(dpois(k, fitted(pois_model))))
nb_freq   <- sapply(0:max_y, function(k)
  mean(dnbinom(k, mu = fitted(nb_model), size = nb_model$theta)))

freq_df <- data.frame(
  absences   = rep(0:max_y, 3),
  proportion = c(obs_freq, pois_freq, nb_freq),
  source     = rep(c("Observed", "Poisson", "Negative Binomial"), each = max_y + 1)
)

ggplot(freq_df, aes(x = absences, y = proportion)) +
  geom_col(data = subset(freq_df, source == "Observed"),
           fill = "grey75", color = "black") +
  geom_line(data = subset(freq_df, source != "Observed"),
            aes(color = source, linetype = source), linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = subset(freq_df, source != "Observed"),
             aes(color = source), size = 1.8) +
  labs(x = "Number of Absences", y = "Proportion of Students",
       color = "Model", linetype = "Model") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

### 4.5 Final model: incidence rate ratios

```{r irr}
nb_coef <- summary(nb_model)$coefficients

irr_tab <- data.frame(
  Estimate = nb_coef[, 1],
  SE       = nb_coef[, 2],
  IRR      = exp(nb_coef[, 1]),
  CI_Lower = exp(nb_coef[, 1] - 1.96 * nb_coef[, 2]),
  CI_Upper = exp(nb_coef[, 1] + 1.96 * nb_coef[, 2]),
  p_value  = nb_coef[, 4]
)
kable(irr_tab, digits = 3, caption = "Table 5: Negative binomial incidence rate ratios")
```

### 4.6 Linearity of Walc

```{r walc-linear}
nb_factor <- glm.nb(absences ~ factor(Walc) + studytime + failures + sex + age + school,
                    data = student)
anova(nb_model, nb_factor)
```

### 4.7 Diagnostics

```{r fig4, fig.cap="Figure 4: Pearson residuals vs. log fitted values (negative binomial)"}
diag_df <- data.frame(
  fitted  = fitted(nb_model),
  pearson = residuals(nb_model, type = "pearson")
)

ggplot(diag_df, aes(x = log(fitted), y = pearson)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, method = "loess", color = "red") +
  labs(x = "log(Fitted Values)", y = "Pearson Residuals") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r influence}
cooks <- cooks.distance(nb_model)
sum(cooks > 4 / nrow(student))
head(sort(cooks, decreasing = TRUE))
```
